parsed.why: Capital district: no local bathroom ban and a non-targeting local regime, but the national legislature's facility restriction applies directly there, local protections are overridable, and December 2024 arrests occurred at the legislature itself. National document/entry regime still caps it.

Adds its own complaint-driven bathroom and locker-room ban in schools and government buildings, with a public reporting form and a surgery/records defence no out-of-state visitor can meet. Private venues exempt, but a documented traveller-facing exposure sits atop the hostile national regime.

No bathroom ban of its own; gender-identity discrimination banned in accommodations since 2013 with hate-crime enhancement; low-risk tier. Residual gaps (panic-defence bill unresolved, no enforcement data) are open questions, not exposures. National border and document regime still applies.

Constitutional equal-protection amendment, accommodation protections, X markers without medical proof, statutory inmate protections and insurer coverage; ranked one tier below the top, with shortfalls that are resident-facing rather than visitor-facing.

Most-protective tier: accommodation statute actually covering hotels, restaurants and venues, gender-neutral single-user bathrooms, shield laws protecting trans travellers against out-of-state action, panic defence abolished. Only the shared national document/entry regime limits it.
